title: This Geyser Shoots Water 300 Feet in the Air

scenes.text: There's a geyser that shoots water 300 feet into the air.
It's Steamboat Geyser in Yellowstone, the tallest active geyser in the world.
One eruption can release roughly ten times the water of Old Faithful.
And nobody can predict when it will blow.
It once stayed quiet for 50 years, then erupted again in 1961.
Three hundred feet. And it decides when.

description:
Steamboat Geyser in Yellowstone sends water more than 300 feet into the air, making it the tallest active geyser in the world.
A major eruption releases around ten times the water of Old Faithful, and the National Park Service calls its timing entirely unpredictable.
Would you wait around to watch it?
first_comment: Bonus: it had a 50-year silent stretch before waking up in 1961. Have you ever seen a geyser erupt?
